transcript: On The Evolutionary Function of Shame joins a growing list of contemporary idea plays well-suited for this age of social and political turmoil. In it, we follow two pairs of Adam and Eves, one who's just ingested the forbidden fruit, the other a twin sister and transgender brother living in the modern day. It’s a play about gender and ethics, and although I thought the writing was sometimes messy or clunky, it was refreshingly bold and smart and dense. I thought I had some very insightful ideas, and my takeaway, beyond the topics brought up explicitly in the dialogue, was just an awareness or allusion to how easily we tend to unknowingly center ourselves in conversations about topics that really have nothing to do with us. I’m not sure if this is meant to be the main takeaway, but I think it's a solid one. For these reasons, I can definitely give this play a pass on it's rough-around-the-edges execution. With that, another program for my collection.
